block.title: RegsProof.v proves valid_alloc CFG simulation, parallel-move compilation and frame separation
block.p: An independent review of RegsProof.v found that its first version proved local step lemmas while the comments and docs credited it with soundness of valid_alloc and compile_pmoves. Its machine state gave every unmapped temporary a private slot instead of a shared frame offset, its move lemmas stopped before cycle scheduling and fuel, its frame lemmas quantified over an abstract list instead of build_rctx, and the default backend build did not compile RegsProof.vo.

RegsProof.v now proves the three verification, scheduling and frame-layout kernels in Regs.v, and nanofil/rocq/backend/Makefile compiles RegsProof.vo with a Print Assumptions check in the default target.

claim.p: valid_alloc_sound proves forward simulation of any register assignment accepted by valid_alloc over multi-block rblock execution traces with shared physical frame slots (Z -> Z indexed by slot_of), multi-definitions, caller-saved call clobbers, simultaneous phi updates and Poll back-edges. compile_pmoves_sound and compile_pmoves_no_todo prove that compile_pmoves never exhausts its 2n + 1 fuel and emits x86-64 mov, movabs and lea lines whose sequential execution equals simul_pmoves across no-op deletion, ready peeling and multiple disjoint cycles. build_rctx_callee_saves_sound and build_rctx_root_lower_slot prove concrete callee-save slot disjointness, prologue/epilogue round-trip and lowers[] root placement for build_rctx. All 163 theorems, lemmas, corollaries and examples are closed under the global context.

block.p: Whole-function x86-64 lowering of function_code_allocated against Semantics.v remains outside proof scope, as stack-homed emission does: Asm.v has no full machine semantics yet, so extraction of rblock use/def/call metadata from fused instructions, FrameSlots.temp_slots non-interference on unmapped temporaries, and body instruction selection stay guarded by tests/regs.sh under FUGC_SCRIBBLE=1 FUGC_VERIFY=1.
